key_concepts: Earth's lithosphere is broken into rigid plates that move slowly.

Convection current is heat transfer driven by temperature and density differences in fluid
Hot, less dense material rises while cooler, denser material sinks.
Mantle convection is driven by heat from Earth's core, especially radioactive decay.
The asthenosphere is the soft upper mantle layer where lithospheric plates float and move.
Rising and sinking magma creates convection cells that move lithospheric plates.
At divergent boundaries, rising magma uplifts and tears apart the lithosphere.
At convergent boundaries, sinking magma pulls tectonic plates downward.
Ridge push, slab pull, and sliding are additional forces that drive plate motion.
